rows.49:3afc: That voice belonged to the spirit that lives in that cherry tree.{p}
rows.49:3b34:
Urged on by the voice, the two of them walked unsteadily to the foot of the cherry tree.
The voice went on.
"...You, too, came here because you believed in my legend, did you not? Then, before you take responsibility, I shall grant the two of you eternal love. Now, exchange a kiss."
Out of nowhere, the cherry tree spirit said that.
What would you do?{p}Would you do as the voice says?
rows.49:3d4c:
Suddenly, four hands shot up out of the earth.
The hands seized the two of them firmly by the ankles.
When the two looked down at their feet in shock, the soil squirmed and heaved up, and two faces emerged from it.
They were, without a doubt, the faces of the two who had been found hanged.
"This is what it means to take responsibility."
The cherry tree spirit said it coldly.
And then the two of them were dragged down into the earth, just like that.
"You have sworn eternal love. But eternity is fragile and fleeting. If you wish to keep it for all eternity, bring me one sacrifice every year..."
Those were the last words the two of them ever heard.{p}
rows.49:3f90:
{a}{f:|}, the hands came out of the ground right about where you're standing now.
They came out from around there.
Heh heh heh heh...
This is the true story behind this tree.
Even now, Hirooka and Orihara offer up one sacrifice every year so they can keep their eternal love.{p}
rows.49:409c: Now, I wonder who it will be this year?{p}{a}{f:|}, it might be you, don't you think?
rows.49:40f0: Say the story is a lie
rows.49:4108: Say we should go back to the club room now
rows.49:4128:
A lie?
You're saying my story is a lie?
Why?
It isn't a lie.
If you say things like that, you'll get yourself killed.
You'll be cursed.
No, you're already cursed.{p}
rows.49:41cc: You're a cursed child.{p}Ah ha ha ha ha...
rows.49:4204: Tell her to stop and grab her
rows.49:4234:
What are you doing?
...Stop that, would you?{p}
rows.49:426c:
Heh heh heh heh...
You moved, didn't you?
Do you remember your promise to me?
I told you not to move until my story was over, didn't I?
My story isn't over yet.
And yet you broke your promise.
You see, I absolutely hate it when people break their promises to me.
And so does the cherry tree spirit.
Because you broke your promise, I've been set free.
So I'll tell you.{p}
rows.49:43c8:
...The truth is, every year, the student who's to become the sacrifice always has a dream.
A dream of Hirooka and Orihara.
And that's how they learn the legend of the cherry tree.
And that they're going to be the sacrifice, too.
Within a week of the dream, the dreamer is called away, they say.
Lured by the two of them, the dreamer hangs themselves while asleep, apparently.
Yes, this year, the one who had the dream was me.
That's why I know.
The legend of the cherry tree.
And in that dream, they taught me all sorts of things.
That there was just one single way for me to save myself.{p}
rows.49:4598:
It's to make someone else take your place.
Anyone will do: you tell them the story of the cherry tree you saw in your dream.
When you do, you make them promise not to scream and not to move from where they are.
Then, if they break that promise, they become your substitute.{p}
rows.49:4700:
Because I still want to live, for a long, long time.
I want to enjoy my life.
For that, I'll do anything.
{a}{f:|}, you'll have the dream soon, too.
The dream of the cherry tree.
When that happens, make sure you remember that you had it.
And then, within a week, tell someone.
If you do, this time that person will take your place.
If you die, I'll grieve for you.
...But that's impossible, isn't it?
If you die, no one will know you ever existed.
Your very existence will vanish from this world, after all.
Even if I wanted to grieve for you, I couldn't.
...Good luck, {a}{f:|}.
Don't hold it against me.
Just think of it as fate...{p}
rows.49:4a30:
I'm sorry, but this is a story I can only tell to people who've made me that promise.
As for why, you'd only understand by hearing the story, and that's something I can't tell you.
That's how frightening a story it is.
So, I'm afraid I can't tell it to you.
But if you ever want to hear it, let me know.
When you do, don't be shy. Just say, "I promise, so please tell me."
I'll tell it to you anytime.
So that's as far as my story goes...
Now, shall we go back to the club room?{p}
rows.49:4bd8:
That's right, it's just as the name says.
Exactly that.
Simple, isn't it?
But you know, the story of this cherry tree isn't as simple as you all think.{p}
rows.49:4c68:
I've heard that rumor before, too.
If I remember right, someone tried to hang themselves from that cherry tree, but survived.
And I heard that while they were unconscious, they had a near-death experience.
Apparently they got within one step of heaven, but, well, a rumor is just a rumor.
Anyway, it's just as the name says.
Yes, the Hanging Cherry...
But you know, the story of this cherry tree isn't as simple as you all think.{p}
rows.49:4ea0:
So you're saying you don't need to hear my story anymore?
I see...
But you know, at the start you promised me you wouldn't move until my story was over.
If I stop my story here, you'll never be able to move from this spot.
You're laughing like that, but...{p}
rows.49:4fb8:
Heh heh heh.
I'll tell you something good.{p}
rows.49:52ac:
Hirooka flew into a rage.
And who could blame him?
If anyone saw the ritual, the couple would meet a miserable end.
On impulse, Hirooka ran straight at the girl.
Not that he had any purpose in mind.
His head was simply in turmoil.
And Hirooka caught the girl.{p}
rows.49:53bc:
"Why did you have to look?!
If it weren't for you, it would've worked!"
Before he knew it, Hirooka was choking the girl by the neck.
"S-stop it!"
At Orihara's voice, Hirooka came to his senses and noticed the girl hanging limp in his arms.
She wasn't breathing.
What a terrible thing he had done.{p}
rows.49:54f8:
"Wh-what do we do?"
Orihara asked in a trembling voice.
Seeing her so frightened, Hirooka hit on an idea.
To secretly bury the girl beneath the cherry tree.
He couldn't bear for Orihara to become an accomplice to murder, and he couldn't bear being caught and separated from her, either.
Orihara was shocked by Hirooka's proposal.
But in the end, she decided to help.
That's what a woman in love is like, isn't it?{p}
rows.49:5664:
Working together, the two of them somehow managed to bury the girl.
It's a strange thing, but it felt as though cooperating like that had made the bond between them stronger.{p}
rows.49:5708:
But some time after that, Hirooka started acting strange.
He grew distant somehow, and avoided Orihara.
They'd always gone home together, but now he'd vanish on his own.
Puzzled, Orihara tried to ask him about it.
But he just evaded her questions.
The girl had been declared missing, so there should have been nothing to worry about.{p}
rows.49:5850:
Then one day after school, Orihara followed Hirooka.
And what do you know, he went to that cherry tree.
What could he be up to?
Orihara drew closer, and the next moment she felt as if she'd been doused with ice water.{p}
rows.49:592c: Why? Because the one waiting for him beneath the cherry tree was the girl who should have been dead.{p}
rows.49:5988:
Hirooka happily took the girl in his arms.
And then he kissed her.
Orihara was shaken.
Not so much because the dead girl was there, but because Hirooka had kissed someone else.
So before she knew it, she rushed out.
Lunging at him, she shoved Hirooka hard in the back.{p}
rows.49:5aa4:
Caught off guard, Hirooka staggered and slammed his head hard against the cherry tree.
There was a dull, sickening sound.{p}
rows.49:5b18:
When Hirooka fell, the trunk of the cherry tree was smeared thick with blood.
...He must have hit it in just the wrong spot.
Hirooka was dead.
As Orihara stood there dumbstruck, the girl jeered and laughed at her.
"Serves you right! That's your punishment for killing me. As if I'd let you two be the only ones who get to be happy!"
With a shrill laugh, the girl melted away and vanished.
But by then, Orihara could no longer hear a thing.
Killing her beloved Hirooka must have been an unbearable shock.{p}
rows.49:5cd4:
...The next day, Orihara was found dead, hanging from a branch of the cherry tree.
At her feet, they say, Hirooka's body had been laid out.{p}
rows.49:5d74:
This is the true story behind this tree.
But actually, there's more to it.
The two of them, who in the end were brought to misery just as the legend said, became evil spirits, they say.
And it seems they convinced themselves that if they offered sacrifices to this tree, their love would surely be fulfilled.
Ever since then, every year, one person dies beneath this cherry tree.
As a sacrifice for the love of Orihara and Hirooka.{p}
rows.49:5f44:
"Maybe we should explain what happened..."
"Yes, maybe we should..."
The two of them started walking toward the other couple.
The other pair seemed shaken, too, and even by moonlight alone, the two could sense it.
Each time that wave of agitation reached them from the other side, their steps grew heavier.
It was Hirooka who finally couldn't stand the situation any longer.{p}
rows.49:6088:
"I wish we hadn't run away back then. If I was going to regret it this much, I should have apologized right then..."
Then Hirooka told Orihara that tomorrow they should find the other couple and apologize.
She agreed with him, saying that would be best.
The two of them would find the couple tomorrow and apologize.
And they parted, promising that the following night, at last, they would once again confirm their love for each other.{p}
rows.49:61d4:
"It was an unfortunate thing, sure, but it's not our fault. Besides, if we'd been a little earlier, we might have been the ones who got seen."
At Hirooka's words, Orihara's face stiffened.
"B-but... then I feel so sorry for those two..."
"Orihara! You matter more to me than some people I don't even know. Let's just forget about it."
The more fervently Hirooka spoke, the more Orihara's face stiffened.
"The Hirooka I love isn't that kind of person. Let's go back and apologize."
When Orihara pressed him, Hirooka reluctantly nodded.
And so they went back to the cherry tree.{p}
rows.49:643c:
............But it was already too late.
Beneath the cherry tree, a boy and a girl lay dead.
They must have been afraid of the misfortune to come.
Two bodies lit by the moonlight, holding hands like the lovers they were.
Orihara's heart filled with regret.
If it was going to come to this, they should never have run.
But Hirooka, it seems, was thinking about something else.
"If anyone finds us here, we're done for. Let's hurry home."
Orihara couldn't believe her ears.
But Hirooka just turned and briskly started for home.{p}
rows.49:65e0:
"W-wait!"
Just as Orihara started to go after him...
rows.49:662c: There was a strange swishing, slithering sound.{p}
rows.49:6670:
When she turned around, the branches of the cherry tree were writhing like whips!
The branches came at Orihara like living things with wills of their own.
"Help me!"
Orihara clung to Hirooka.
And Hirooka shoved her away.
"You'll get me caught, too!"
In that instant, Orihara felt she understood who Hirooka really was.
That he cared only about himself, that as long as he was saved, nothing else mattered.
And then, somehow, all her strength drained away.
She felt like a fool for having loved such a man.
Orihara stopped where she stood, and the cherry tree wrapped around her neck and squeezed.
And whip-like branches shot out at the fleeing Hirooka's neck, too.
A branch went straight through Hirooka's throat.{p}
